title: He was hiding.
paragraphs:
He was hiding.
God called him a warrior.
Let that tension sit.
Because some of you are in a season where your reality and God’s voice don’t match.

You feel small.
God speaks destiny.
You see fear.
God declares purpose.

Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress—doing it in secret, in fear, in survival mode (Judges 6:11).
This wasn’t a man ready for battle.
This was a man trying not to be seen.
And then heaven interrupted.
“The LORD is with you, mighty warrior.” (Judges 6:12)

Not “future warrior.”
Not “potential warrior.”
Mighty. Warrior.

Right there.
In the hiding place.
Here’s the part we don’t talk about enough:

Gideon didn’t respond with confidence.
He responded with questions.
“If the LORD is with us, why has all this happened?” (Judges 6:13)

That’s not rebellion.
That’s real.
Pain asking honest questions.

Some scholars interpret Gideon’s response as doubt…
Others see it as wounded faith trying to breathe again.
But watch this—

God didn’t cancel him.
God stayed.
Then Gideon says something even deeper:
“My clan is the weakest… and I am the least.” (Judges 6:15)
Translation?
“I’m not built for this.”
And God’s answer wasn’t, “No, you’re actually strong.”
God said:
“I will be with you.” (Judges 6:16)
That’s the shift.

Your calling is not built on your strength.
It’s built on His presence.
But here’s what will shake you—
God intentionally reduced Gideon’s army.
Why?
“Lest Israel boast… ‘My own hand has saved me.’” (Judges 7:2)

God will sometimes strip your resources
to protect His glory in your story.

That business plan.
That relationship.
That confidence you leaned on.
Gone.

Not to destroy you—
but to reveal Him.
And Gideon?
Still afraid.
God literally sends him to overhear the enemy’s dream just to strengthen his heart (Judges 7:10–15).
That’s the kind of God we serve.

He doesn’t just command courage.
He builds it in you.

Step by step.
Grace by grace.
But don’t miss this—
The victory didn’t come through swords.
It came through obedience.

Torches.
Clay jars.
Trumpets.

Weak strategy.
Strong God.
And in one night, Midian collapsed (Judges 7:20–22).
But here’s the deeper Gospel thread—
Gideon’s story is not about a man becoming brave.

It’s about God choosing the weak
to shame the strong.
“God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong.” (1 Corinthians 1:27)
Sound familiar?
Because centuries later, another “unlikely” Deliverer came.

Not in power.
But in humility.

Not with an army.
But with a cross.
Jesus Christ.

Where Gideon broke oppression for a season,
Jesus broke sin forever.

Where Gideon needed signs,
Jesus became the sign.

Where Gideon was called “mighty” before he felt it,
Jesus was called “King” before the world believed it.

And through His death and resurrection,
He didn’t just win battles—
He won you back.
So if you’re reading this feeling:

Unqualified.
Overlooked.
Afraid.
Still hiding.
Listen carefully—
God is not waiting for you to become strong.
He’s calling you while you’re still in the winepress.
Because grace doesn’t start when you’re ready.
It starts when you surrender.
You don’t need 32,000 reasons to believe in yourself.
You just need one reason to trust Him:
“The LORD is with you.” (Judges 6:12)
That’s enough.
And maybe… just maybe…

The thing you’re most insecure about
is the exact place where God will reveal His power the loudest.
Because you are not disqualified.
You are being prepared.

From hiding to calling.
From fear to faith.
From weakness to witness.
Because of Jesus.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
